s01-title: Sign in with your company IDP. The company directory manages the accounts.
s02-login: One button: Acme Corp SSO. The password stays at the IDP; Astra gets only an OIDC code. This Linh is an IDP user, not STMS's.
s03-flow: SP initiated flow: Desk, Keycloak, IDP, and back. The realms speak real SAML two point oh; the Desk speaks only OIDC with Keycloak.
s04-assertion: The IDP signs an assertion with the user's groups. Keycloak maps them to tenants acme editor in the token; Astra reads the role there.
s05-desk: Linh Vo signs in as acme editor and creates an article. No SSO code in the kernel; DocType permissions apply as for local users.
s06-tamper: Change one word of the assertion in transit. The signature breaks, and Keycloak stops the flow. No code, so nobody signs in.
s07-discovery: SCIM two point oh, at scim v two. The tenant comes only from Keycloak's scim tenant claim on the client, never from the request.
s08-create: POST creates the user: two oh one. A repeat user name gets four oh nine. New users have no role, so no rights yet.
s09-role: Groups are roles. Join the editor group, sign in again, and the user can create articles. Changes apply at the next sign-in or refresh.
s10-deactivate: Setting active to false blocks sign-in at once. Tokens already issued stay valid until they expire, since Astra verifies JWTs offline.
s11-failclosed: Fail closed: a globex token can't reach acme users. Errors follow RFC seventy-six forty-four; deleted users are gone.
s12-honest: To be accurate: the IDP is a local Keycloak realm, not Okta or Entra. SP initiated only; no Single Logout or SCIM Bulk yet.
s99-recap: Recap: sign-in through the IDP, accounts provisioned with SCIM. Next: Roadmap.
s13-outro: Astra. One platform, every business process. Open source.
